description: Held-out quiz tasks — never sampled by the flywheel curriculum. `objective` states a signature and describes behaviour; the assertions live in `holdout_test`, which the generator never sees (graded by core.holdout.grade_against_holdout). v1 pasted the finished implementation AND its assertion into every objective, so the quiz measured transcription.

tasks.title: fib
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def fib(n: int) -> int

Return the nth Fibonacci number, counting from fib(0) == 0 and fib(1) == 1, so each later term is the sum of the two before it.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert fib(0) == 0
assert fib(1) == 1
assert fib(2) == 1
assert fib(10) == 55
assert fib(15) == 610
print('ok')

tasks.title: is_prime
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def is_prime(n: int) -> bool

Return the bool True when n is a prime number. Anything below 2 is not prime.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert is_prime(17) is True
assert is_prime(15) is False
assert is_prime(2) is True
assert is_prime(1) is False
assert is_prime(0) is False
assert is_prime(-7) is False
print('ok')

tasks.title: rotate_left
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def rotate_left(xs: list, k: int) -> list

Return a new list with the elements of xs rotated k places to the left, so the element at index k comes first and the ones before it move to the end. k may be larger than the list. An empty list returns an empty list.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert rotate_left([1, 2, 3, 4], 1) == [2, 3, 4, 1]
assert rotate_left([1, 2, 3, 4], 0) == [1, 2, 3, 4]
assert rotate_left([1, 2, 3, 4], 4) == [1, 2, 3, 4]
assert rotate_left([1, 2, 3], 5) == [3, 1, 2]
assert rotate_left([], 3) == []
print('ok')

tasks.title: anagram
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def anagram(a: str, b: str) -> bool

Return the bool True when a and b use exactly the same letters with the same multiplicities. Ignore letter case and ignore spaces; every other character counts.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert anagram('listen', 'silent') is True
assert anagram('Dormitory', 'dirty room') is True
assert anagram('abc', 'abd') is False
assert anagram('aab', 'abb') is False
assert anagram('', '') is True
print('ok')

tasks.title: running_sum
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def running_sum(xs: list) -> list

Return a list of the same length whose ith element is the sum of xs[0..i] inclusive. An empty list returns an empty list.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert running_sum([1, 2, 3]) == [1, 3, 6]
assert running_sum([]) == []
assert running_sum([5]) == [5]
assert running_sum([1, -1, 2]) == [1, 0, 2]
print('ok')

tasks.title: deep_get
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def deep_get(d: dict, keys: list, default=None)

Walk the nested dict d following each key in keys in order and return the value found. Return default as soon as the walk hits something that is not a dict or a key that is missing. An empty key list returns d itself.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert deep_get({'a': {'b': 2}}, ['a', 'b']) == 2
assert deep_get({'a': {'b': 2}}, ['a', 'z']) is None
assert deep_get({'a': {'b': 2}}, ['a', 'b', 'c'], 'x') == 'x'
assert deep_get({'a': 1}, ['missing'], 0) == 0
assert deep_get({'a': 1}, []) == {'a': 1}
print('ok')

tasks.title: compress
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def compress(s: str) -> str

Run-length encode s: replace each run of one repeated character with that character followed by the length of the run, written as a decimal number. Every run gets a count, including runs of length 1. An empty string returns an empty string.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert compress('aabbb') == 'a2b3'
assert compress('') == ''
assert compress('a') == 'a1'
assert compress('abc') == 'a1b1c1'
assert compress('aaaaaaaaaaa') == 'a11'
print('ok')

tasks.title: matrix_sum
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def matrix_sum(m: list) -> int

m is a list of rows, each row a list of numbers. Return the sum of every element. An empty matrix sums to 0.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert matrix_sum([[1, 2], [3, 4]]) == 10
assert matrix_sum([]) == 0
assert matrix_sum([[]]) == 0
assert matrix_sum([[5]]) == 5
assert matrix_sum([[1, 1, 1], [-3]]) == 0
print('ok')

tasks.title: longest_word
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def longest_word(s: str) -> str

Split s on whitespace and return the longest word. On a tie return the one that appears first. A string with no words returns an empty string.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert longest_word('a bb ccc') == 'ccc'
assert longest_word('') == ''
assert longest_word('   ') == ''
assert longest_word('aa bb') == 'aa'
assert longest_word('one') == 'one'
print('ok')

tasks.title: set_bits
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def set_bits(n: int) -> int

Return how many bits are set to 1 in the binary representation of the non-negative integer n. set_bits(0) is 0.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert set_bits(7) == 3
assert set_bits(0) == 0
assert set_bits(1) == 1
assert set_bits(8) == 1
assert set_bits(255) == 8
print('ok')

tasks.title: interleave
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def interleave(a: list, b: list) -> list

Return one list that alternates a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1], ... When one list runs out, append the rest of the longer one in order.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert interleave([1, 2], [9]) == [1, 9, 2]
assert interleave([], []) == []
assert interleave([1], [2]) == [1, 2]
assert interleave([], [1, 2]) == [1, 2]
assert interleave([1, 2, 3], [4]) == [1, 4, 2, 3]
print('ok')

tasks.title: normalize_path
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def normalize_path(parts: list) -> str

parts is a list of path segments. Build an absolute POSIX path from them: skip empty segments and '.', let '..' remove the previous segment (and do nothing at the root), and join what remains with '/' after a leading '/'. No segments left means '/'.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert normalize_path(['a', 'b', '..', 'c']) == '/a/c'
assert normalize_path([]) == '/'
assert normalize_path(['..']) == '/'
assert normalize_path(['a', '.', 'b']) == '/a/b'
assert normalize_path(['a', '', 'b']) == '/a/b'
print('ok')

tasks.title: median
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def median(xs: list)

Return the median of the numbers in xs: the middle value once sorted when the count is odd, and the mean of the two middle values when it is even. An empty list returns None. Do not modify the caller's list.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert median([1, 3, 2]) == 2
assert median([]) is None
assert median([1, 2, 3, 4]) == 2.5
assert median([7]) == 7
xs = [3, 1, 2]
assert median(xs) == 2
assert xs == [3, 1, 2]
print('ok')

tasks.title: group_by_len
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def group_by_len(words: list) -> dict

Return a dict mapping each word length to the list of words of that length, keeping the order they appear in the input. An empty input returns an empty dict.

tasks.title: stable_unique
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def stable_unique(xs: list) -> list

Return the elements of xs with duplicates removed, keeping the first occurrence of each value and the original order.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert stable_unique([2, 1, 2, 3, 1]) == [2, 1, 3]
assert stable_unique([]) == []
assert stable_unique([1, 1, 1]) == [1]
assert stable_unique(['b', 'a', 'b']) == ['b', 'a']
print('ok')

tasks.title: caesar
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def caesar(s: str, k: int) -> str

Shift every ASCII letter of s forward by k positions through the alphabet, wrapping from z back to a, and preserve each letter's case. Leave every non-letter character untouched. k may be negative.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert caesar('ab', 1) == 'bc'
assert caesar('z', 1) == 'a'
assert caesar('Zebra!', 1) == 'Afcsb!'
assert caesar('abc', 0) == 'abc'
assert caesar('bc', -1) == 'ab'
print('ok')

tasks.title: transpose
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def transpose(m: list) -> list

m is a rectangular matrix as a list of row lists. Return its transpose as a list of lists, so element [i][j] of the result is element [j][i] of m. An empty matrix returns an empty list.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert transpose([[1, 2], [3, 4]]) == [[1, 3], [2, 4]]
assert transpose([]) == []
assert transpose([[1, 2, 3]]) == [[1], [2], [3]]
assert transpose([[1], [2]]) == [[1, 2]]
print('ok')

tasks.title: balanced_parens
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def balanced_parens(s: str) -> bool

Return the bool True when every '(' in s is closed by a later ')' and no ')' appears before its opener. Characters other than parentheses are ignored. An empty string is balanced.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert balanced_parens('(())') is True
assert balanced_parens('(()') is False
assert balanced_parens(')(') is False
assert balanced_parens('') is True
assert balanced_parens('a(b)c') is True
print('ok')

tasks.title: merge_dicts
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def merge_dicts(a: dict, b: dict) -> dict

Return a new dict holding the entries of both. Where a key is in both, b's value wins. Neither input may be modified.

tasks.title: second_largest
tasks.objective:
Write only Python, no markdown.

Implement:

def second_largest(xs: list)

Return the second largest DISTINCT value in xs, so repeats of the maximum do not count. Return None when there are fewer than two distinct values.
tasks.holdout_test:
assert second_largest([1, 5, 5, 3]) == 3
assert second_largest([1, 2]) == 1
assert second_largest([4, 4, 4]) is None
assert second_largest([]) is None
assert second_largest([9]) is None
print('ok')
